commands.name: git
commands.summary: Distributed version control system for tracking and managing code changes.
commands.risk_reason: Force push and history rewrite on shared branches can overwrite collaborators' work.
cautions: `git push --force` and other history rewrites can erase teammates’ commits; prefer --force-with-lease.
`git reset --hard` and `git clean -fd` delete uncommitted/untracked work that cannot be recovered.
Check `git status` and `git remote -v` before pushing so you do not push to the wrong remote or branch.
commands.explanation: git tracks file changes through commits and supports branching and merging. The working directory, staging area (index), and repository are distinct zones. Remote operations interact with upstream repositories.

examples.desc: Visualize full branch history as a compact decorated graph

examples.cmd: git stash push -m 'WIP: feature-x' && git checkout main
examples.desc: Stash current work and switch to main
Show changes in src/api/ over the last 3 commits

safer.why: Force push that refuses to overwrite commits you have not seen.

commands.pro_tip: Use `git reflog` to recover lost commits after a bad reset or rebase — git keeps unreachable commits for ~90 days.

commands.name: git log
commands.summary: Browse, filter, and format Git commit history.
commands.risk_reason: Read-only history viewer.
commands.explanation: git log displays the commit history with flexible formatting. Supports filtering by author, date, path, and content. The --graph flag visualizes branch topology. A well-formatted git log is essential for code review, debugging, and release management.

flags.desc: Show file change stats per commit

examples.desc: Visual branch history for all branches
Find when a specific string was added/removed
Full history of a file including renames

commands.pro_tip: Add `git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all` as an alias `git lg` — the graph view reveals merge topology that linear history completely hides.

commands.name: git stash
commands.summary: Temporarily save and restore uncommitted work.
commands.risk_reason: Stashes can be accidentally dropped; they're not a backup.
commands.explanation: git stash saves your working directory changes and index to a stack, letting you switch contexts cleanly and restore later. Supports multiple stashes, partial stashing with -p, and stashing untracked files with -u.

flags.desc: Apply most recent stash and remove it

examples.cmd: git stash push -m 'WIP: refactor auth module'

commands.pro_tip: Use `git stash push -u -m 'description'` to include untracked files — otherwise new files you've created stay in the working tree and may contaminate the branch you switch to.

commands.name: git rebase
commands.summary: Reapply commits on top of another base commit; rewrite history.
commands.risk_reason: Rewrites commit history; dangerous on shared/public branches.
cautions: Rewrites commit hashes — never rebase commits that others have already pulled.
Wrongly resolved conflicts during a rebase silently drop changes; review with `git diff ORIG_HEAD`.
You can abort an unfinished rebase with `git rebase --abort`; afterwards recover with `git reflog`.
commands.explanation: git rebase replays commits from one branch on top of another, producing a linear history. Interactive rebase (-i) lets you squash, reorder, edit, and drop commits. Never rebase public/shared branches — it rewrites history and forces conflicts for others.

flags.desc: Interactive rebase: edit, squash, reorder commits

examples.desc: Rebase current branch on top of main
Interactively clean up last 5 commits before PR
Safely cancel a rebase in progress

safer.why: Leave a pointer to the old history so you can always reset to it.
Find the pre-rebase commit if something goes wrong.

commands.pro_tip: Use interactive rebase (`git rebase -i HEAD~N`) before raising PRs to squash fixup commits and write meaningful commit messages — keeps the project history clean and reviewable.

commands.name: git cherry-pick
commands.summary: Apply specific commits from one branch to another.
commands.risk_reason: Can create duplicate commits and cause conflicts.
cautions: Creates a duplicate commit with a new hash — later merges may conflict or apply the change twice.
Use -x to record the original commit hash in the message for traceability.
commands.explanation: git cherry-pick applies the changes introduced by specific commits (by hash) to the current branch, creating new commits with the same changes. Useful for backporting fixes to release branches without merging all changes.

flags.desc: Apply changes without creating a commit
Append original commit hash to message

examples.desc: Apply commit abc1234 to current branch

commands.pro_tip: Use `git cherry-pick -x` to include the original commit hash in the message — creates a paper trail linking the backport to the original fix, invaluable for tracking.

commands.name: git add
commands.risk_reason: Only modifies the index.
cautions: `git add .` can stage secrets, .env files and build output — check git status/diff --staged.
Add .gitignore entries for credentials.
commands.explanation: Stages files for the next commit. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

commands.name: git commit
commands.risk_reason: Local only until pushed.
cautions: Never commit secrets — rotate any key that was committed even if you remove it later.
--amend on pushed commits requires a force push.
--no-verify skips pre-commit/security hooks.
commands.explanation: Creates a commit from the index. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

flags.caution: Changes history; don’t amend pushed commits.

commands.name: git push
commands.risk_reason: Publishes changes; --force can overwrite others’ commits.
cautions: Check `git remote -v` and the branch before pushing.
Never force-push shared branches (main, release).
--delete removes a remote branch for everyone.
Pushed secrets are public history — rotate them.
commands.explanation: Sends local commits to a remote branch. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

commands.name: git pull
commands.risk_reason: Merges remote changes into your branch; conflicts and surprise merges.
cautions: Uncommitted changes may conflict — stash or commit first.
Prefer `git fetch` + review, or --ff-only.
commands.explanation: Fetch + merge (or rebase with --rebase).

commands.name: git fetch
commands.risk_reason: Updates remote-tracking branches only.
commands.explanation: Gets objects and refs without modifying your working tree.

commands.name: git clone
commands.risk_reason: Downloads code that may run hooks/scripts later.
cautions: Review untrusted repositories before running their scripts/Makefiles.
Embedded credentials in URLs end up in .git/config.
commands.explanation: Creates a local copy of a repo. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

commands.name: git status
commands.risk_reason: Read-only.
commands.explanation: Shows staged, unstaged and untracked files.

commands.name: git diff
commands.risk_reason: Read-only.
cautions: Diffs may include secrets — don’t paste them publicly.
commands.explanation: Compares working tree, index and commits.

commands.name: git merge
commands.risk_reason: Creates merge commits and conflicts.
cautions: Check you are on the right branch before merging.
Resolve conflicts carefully; run tests before pushing.
commands.explanation: Integrates another branch into the current one.

safer.why: Merge without committing to inspect first

commands.name: git reset
commands.risk_reason: --hard permanently discards uncommitted work; resetting pushed history needs a force push.
cautions: `git reset --hard` deletes uncommitted modifications with no recovery.
Resetting shared branches rewrites history for everyone.
Recover lost commits with `git reflog` (within ~90 days).
commands.explanation: Moves the current branch to another commit; --soft keeps changes staged, --mixed unstages, --hard discards.

examples.desc: Undo the last commit, keep changes

commands.name: git revert
commands.summary: Undo a commit with a new commit
commands.risk_reason: Creates a new commit; history is preserved.
cautions: Reverting a merge needs -m 1 and complicates re-merging.
commands.explanation: Applies the inverse of a commit — safe for shared branches.

commands.name: git checkout
commands.risk_reason: Can overwrite uncommitted changes in files.
cautions: `git checkout -- file` or `git checkout .` irreversibly discards local edits.
commands.explanation: Older multi-purpose command; prefer git switch / git restore.

commands.name: git switch
commands.risk_reason: Fails instead of overwriting uncommitted changes.
commands.explanation: Modern replacement for branch switching.

commands.name: git restore
commands.risk_reason: Discards working-tree changes without confirmation.
cautions: Without --staged, edits are lost permanently.
commands.explanation: Restores paths from the index or a commit; --staged unstages.

safer.why: Look at what you would lose

commands.name: git branch
commands.risk_reason: -D deletes branches including unmerged work.
cautions: Prefer -d; -D discards unmerged commits.
commands.explanation: Manages local branches. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

commands.name: git tag
commands.risk_reason: Tags can be moved or deleted remotely.
cautions: Don’t move published tags; consumers pin them.
commands.explanation: Marks releases. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

commands.name: git remote
commands.risk_reason: Wrong remote URL sends code to the wrong place.
cautions: Check the URL before pushing proprietary code.
commands.explanation: Lists and edits remote repositories. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

commands.name: git reflog
commands.risk_reason: Read-only.
commands.explanation: Lets you recover commits lost to resets or rebases.

commands.name: git clean
commands.risk_reason: Deletes untracked files permanently.
cautions: Always run with -n first.
-x deletes ignored files such as .env and local configs.
commands.explanation: Removes files not tracked by git. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

commands.name: git bisect
commands.summary: Binary search for a bad commit
commands.risk_reason: Changes HEAD while running.
cautions: Commit or stash work first; always run `git bisect reset` when done.
commands.explanation: Finds the commit that introduced a bug. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

commands.name: git blame
commands.risk_reason: Read-only.
commands.explanation: Annotates lines with the last commit. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

commands.name: git submodule
commands.risk_reason: Detached HEADs and pinned commits cause surprises.
cautions: Submodules may point at untrusted repositories.
commands.explanation: Initialises and updates submodules. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

commands.name: git worktree
commands.risk_reason: Extra directories to clean up.
commands.explanation: Check out several branches at once. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

commands.name: git config
commands.risk_reason: Can store credentials or alter hooks/aliases.
cautions: Credential helpers storing plaintext are insecure; use a keychain.
Aliases can execute shell commands.
commands.explanation: Manages git settings. See the flags and examples below, and run `man git` for the full reference.

commands.name: gh
commands.risk_reason: Acts on your GitHub account (creates PRs, merges, deletes repos).
cautions: `gh repo delete` and `gh pr merge` are irreversible on remotes.
Scopes of your token define the blast radius; use least-privilege tokens.
commands.explanation: Work with PRs, issues and repos from the terminal.
